card: Validates block locator counts against MAX_LOCATOR_SZ in getblocks and getheaders messages before deserializing the hashes. Previously, the size check ran only after deserialization, allowing peers that sent truncated messages with oversized counts to bypass disconnection because generic deserialization failures do not disconnect. The change introduces a distinct exception for limited vector overflows and disconnects the peer upon receiving an oversized count regardless of whether the message was truncated.
evidence: PR description: "A truncated locator advertising an oversized count makes generic vector deserialization fail before the disconnect check, leaving the peer connected."

Commit e327916668: "Use CBlockLocator::LimitedRead to detect the oversized count before allocating hashes. The message handler catches only LimitedVectorExceededError and disconnects the peer. Other deserialization failures keep following the generic non-disconnecting exception path."
problem: Peers sending oversized block locators in getblocks and getheaders are supposed to be disconnected, but the MAX_LOCATOR_SZ check occurred only after full deserialization. A truncated message specifying an oversized count failed in generic vector deserialization before reaching the limit check, causing the message handler to drop the message but leave the peer connected.
summary: Enforces the block locator size limit in incoming getblocks and getheaders messages before allocating and deserializing locator hashes. Introduces a dedicated LimitedVectorExceededError exception to the limited vector deserializer and adds CBlockLocator::LimitedRead to catch oversized locator counts. In net processing, oversized locators now trigger peer disconnection immediately, even if the payload is truncated.
